blocks.title: Edge computing
blocks.text: Edge computing processes data at the edge of the network, near where the data are produced, instead of only in central data centres. This reduces latency, the delay of sending data back and forth, and allows faster, real-time decisions.

In autonomous vehicles, data from sensors and cameras are processed inside the vehicle, so it can react quickly to road conditions. Edge computing also suits smart cities, healthcare monitoring and industrial automation, which need real-time processing (Top Tip).

blocks.prompt: What is the main benefit of edge computing (MCQ 1)? Which is an example of it (MCQ 14)? Which technology processes data at the edge (MCQ 17)?
blocks.explanation: (b) reduced latency; (b) autonomous vehicles; (a) edge computing.

blocks.prompt: What is edge computing and how does it benefit data processing (short question 3)? How does it make autonomous vehicles more efficient (short question 8)? Discuss its advances and benefits (long question 4).
blocks.explanation: Edge computing moves processing close to the data source. Benefits: lower latency and real-time responses; less data sent over the network, saving bandwidth; continued work when the connection is weak; and sensitive data can stay local. In a self-driving car, camera and sensor data are analysed on board in milliseconds, so it can brake or steer at once instead of waiting for a distant data centre. It powers smart cities, patient monitoring and factory automation. The bandwidth and offline points are general knowledge.

items: Edge computing: process near the source; low latency; self-driving cars, smart cities, healthcare.
